clue.text: Tinker on stage, holding online meeting without ado

indicators.note: to hold something is to keep it inside you, so the tinker's name wraps around the meeting

parts.note: Christopher Sly is the drunken tinker in the opening scenes of The Taming of the Shrew
an e-date is a date arranged or held online

explanation.surface: A tinkerer messing about on a theatre stage while holding a video call, all without any fuss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tinker' looks like a verb meaning fiddle about, but it names Shakespeare's tinker, Christopher Sly, who wraps around E-DATE to give SEDATELY.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something sedately means doing it calmly and unhurriedly, with no fuss or commotion.

clue.text: After it's put up on stage, I'm wrong to condemn

indicators.note: in a down entry, one piece sitting on another is written above it
in a down clue, putting something up means writing it from the bottom upwards

parts.note: taken as written, without the apostrophe

indicators.note: letters that are wrong are out of their proper places and must be rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An actor regrets condemning something once it has been staged.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After' just sets the scene; STI sits on top of the rearranged STAGE I'M to make STIGMATISE.
explanation.definitionFit: To stigmatise is to brand someone as disgraceful, a way of publicly denouncing them.

clue.text: Able to identify what's wrong as I do casting badly

indicators.note: something done badly is botched and jumbled, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A director admits to choosing actors poorly and spots what has gone wrong.
explanation.definitionFit: A diagnostic test or tool is one designed to pinpoint a fault or illness.

clue.text: eg Julius Caesar or Coriolanus? Right

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the name of a play, each here being a Shakespeare play

explanation.surface: A quiz question asking what Julius Caesar or Coriolanus is, with the answer confirmed as right.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Right' looks like a quizmaster's approval, but it is the second meaning: a legal claim.
explanation.definitionFit: Julius Caesar and Coriolanus are names of plays, and a title is also a legal claim to ownership.

clue.text: Delights in Tory victory as comedy

parts.note: to delight in something is to love it
when the Conservatives win a British election

explanation.surface: A Conservative supporter relishes an election win as if it were a comedy.
explanation.walkthrough: Tory is the everyday name for Britain's Conservative Party, whose main opponent is the Labour Party.
explanation.definitionFit: Love's Labour's Lost is one of Shakespeare's early comedies, about four lords forswearing women.

clue.text: Assertion from one kind of character heard, found in either part of Twelfth Night

indicators.note: something heard is taken by its sound rather than its spelling

parts.note: a vowel is one kind of letter, letters being characters

parts.words: found in either part of Twelfth Night
parts.note: a playful extra: each word of the title, Twelfth and Night, contains exactly one vowel

explanation.surface: A declaration made by someone in a Shakespeare comedy, appearing in both halves of Twelfth Night.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Character' suggests a role in the play, but here it means a letter of the alphabet.
explanation.definitionFit: An avowal is an open declaration or affirmation, which is a kind of assertion.

clue.text: Romantic message for Veronese gentleman

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a card sent to a sweetheart on 14 February
second meaning: one of the title characters of The Two Gentlemen of Verona

explanation.surface: A love letter sent to a gentleman from Verona.
explanation.definitionFit: A valentine is a love card, and Valentine is one of Shakespeare's Two Gentlemen of Verona.

clue.text: Practice acting in Winter's Tale, initially

indicators.note: one piece sits in between the others, enclosed by them
initially points to the opening letter of each of the play's two title words

parts.note: first letter
an actor who is acting is on, that is on stage
first letter

explanation.surface: A rehearsal for a performance of The Winter's Tale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Practice' looks like a rehearsal, but the definition means habit.
explanation.definitionFit: Wont is an old word for a habit or custom, someone's usual practice.

clue.text: See 4
Quiescent during penultimate part of Macbeth — and of Hamlet

parts.note: during a period means in it
Macbeth has five acts, so its next-to-last part is Act IV

indicators.note: the part before last of Hamlet's name is its second-to-last letter

parts.note: the fifth of the six letters

explanation.surface: A character lies dormant during the later part of Macbeth and of Hamlet too.
explanation.walkthrough: The same phrase is read two ways: for Macbeth the 'part' is an act, for Hamlet it is a letter of the name.
explanation.definitionFit: Something quiescent is still and dormant, which is to say not active.

clue.text: They support arms, weapons linked with arrows in dramatic speech

definitions.meaning: first meaning: bandages hung from the neck to hold up an injured arm

definitions.text: weapons linked with arrows in dramatic speech

explanation.surface: Supporters of armed force pair one weapon with arrows in a stirring theatrical address.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Arms' suggests weaponry alongside the weapons that follow, but the first meaning is about limbs.
explanation.definitionFit: Slings are cloth supports for injured arms and also simple stone-throwing weapons named beside arrows in Hamlet.

clue.text: Novice Romeo crazy about female — tragic hero

indicators.note: about means going round, so the jumbled letters surround the single one
crazy letters have lost their senses and order, so they are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
F is the standard abbreviation for female

explanation.surface: An inexperienced Romeo is besotted with a woman, which makes him a tragic figure.
explanation.walkthrough: Romeo hints at Shakespeare's tragic lover, but he is only letters here.
explanation.definitionFit: Othello, the Moor of Venice is the full title of Shakespeare's tragedy, and its title role is a tragic hero.

clue.text: It's darn hard in initially confused lesson naming writer of A Midsummer Night's Dream

definitions.text: writer of A Midsummer Night's Dream

indicators.note: initially says the mending piece comes first, before the rest is built

parts.note: to darn a sock is to mend it

indicators.note: one letter is placed inside the rearranged word
confused letters are muddled up and must be put in a new order

parts.note: taken as written
H is the pencil-grading abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: A frustrated pupil finds a muddled lesson on the author of A Midsummer Night's Dream very hard going.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'writer' is not Shakespeare: Mendelssohn wrote the famous incidental music for A Midsummer Night's Dream, including the Wedding March.
explanation.definitionFit: Felix Mendelssohn composed the overture and incidental music to A Midsummer Night's Dream, so he wrote a Dream too.

clue.text: One who operates in theatre, not needing screen

definitions.text: One who operates in theatre, not needing screen

parts.note: surface reading: a surgeon working in an operating theatre
setter's reading: a performer working live on stage rather than in film or on television

explanation.surface: A surgeon who works in the operating theatre without needing a screen round the patient.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Operates' and 'theatre' call up surgery; read again, the theatre is a playhouse and the screen is cinema.
explanation.definitionFit: A stage actor performs in live theatre, as opposed to a screen actor who works in film or television.

clue.text: Church's part obvious in sound plot

indicators.note: in sound means the word is taken by how it is pronounced, not spelt

parts.note: obvious means plain or evident
the plot of a play is its story

explanation.surface: A church drama whose storyline is plainly predictable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sound plot' reads as a solid storyline, but 'in sound' governs only the first piece.
explanation.definitionFit: A clerestory is the upper row of windows in a church's nave, letting light in above the aisle roofs.

clue.text: Leading characters in Titus Andronicus spoil the ending in one sense

indicators.note: leading characters are the letters at the front of each word that follows

parts.note: first letters of the five words

explanation.surface: The main roles in Titus Andronicus wreck the play's finale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leading characters' suggests the main roles of the tragedy, but it means initial letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Taste is one of the five senses, alongside sight, hearing, smell and touch.

clue.text: Like lady's protest in play that confounds sexes with vice

indicators.note: to confound is to mix up and throw into disorder, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A scandalous play that blurs gender and wickedness provokes protest from a lady.
explanation.walkthrough: In Hamlet, Gertrude says 'The lady doth protest too much, methinks'; too much means excessive.
explanation.definitionFit: The play-within-a-play queen protests too much, and too much is an overdone, immoderate amount.

clue.text: Appearance with Falstaff's associate producing weapon

parts.note: an air is a manner or appearance, as in an air of confidence
Pistol is one of Falstaff's swaggering cronies in Henry IV Part 2 and The Merry Wives of Windsor
puts the two pieces side by side

explanation.surface: A stage entrance alongside one of Falstaff's sidekicks brings out a gun.
explanation.definitionFit: An air pistol is a handgun firing pellets by compressed air, a kind of weapon.

clue.text: Second member of weird trio having exited? Stop watching

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for second
the three witches of Macbeth are the Weird Sisters
an actor who has exited is off, that is offstage

explanation.surface: The second of Macbeth's three witches leaves the stage, and a viewer stops watching.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Second' looks like a position among the witches, but it is just the abbreviation S.
explanation.definitionFit: To switch off is to turn off the television, or simply lose interest and stop paying attention.

clue.text: Earl's son in King Lear appearing in tattered garment

indicators.note: appearing in says the answer shows up inside the words that follow

parts.note: runs across the join of the two words

explanation.surface: A nobleman's son in King Lear turns up dressed in rags.
explanation.walkthrough: Fittingly, Edgar spends much of King Lear disguised in rags as Poor Tom.
explanation.definitionFit: Edgar is the legitimate son of the Earl of Gloucester in King Lear.

clue.text: Check power, sets, scripts for film adaptations

parts.note: to screen candidates is to check them
P is the physics symbol for power
to set a table is to lay it

explanation.surface: A film crew checks the electricity supply, the stage sets and the scripts before shooting.
explanation.definitionFit: Screenplays are the written scripts from which films are shot, often adapted from plays.

clue.text: Superficially cut, like Antony and Cleopatra or Romeo and Juliet, we hear

indicators.note: we hear means the word is taken by its sound, not by its spelling

parts.words: like Antony and Cleopatra or Romeo and Juliet
parts.note: each title joins two lovers as a couple

explanation.surface: Shakespeare's love tragedies given a light trim, by the sound of it.
explanation.definitionFit: To pare is to trim away the outer layer, so pared means cut at the surface only.

clue.text: Dismiss, in a way, from Richard's royal house

definitions.meaning: first meaning: in cricket, to ... a batsman is to bowl them out with a yorker, a ball pitching at their feet
second meaning: Richard III belonged to the House of ...

explanation.surface: Someone is thrown out of King Richard's palace.
explanation.walkthrough: Cricket is the key to the first meaning: a yorker is a delivery aimed at the batter's toes.
explanation.definitionFit: York is a cricketing verb for bowling a batter out, and the dynasty to which Richard III belonged.

clue.text: Shakespeare, as opposed to 7

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the playwright's first name, short for William
second meaning: the answer to 7 can be read as the contraction for ... not, and its opposite is ...

explanation.walkthrough: The 7 answer means habit, but read as a contraction it is the negative form of the verb, whose positive is this.
explanation.definitionFit: Will is Shakespeare's familiar first name and also the positive auxiliary set against its negative contraction.

clue.text: Famous actor exchanging last two parts for a role in Twelfth Night

indicators.note: exchanging the final pair of letters means swapping them out for something else

parts.note: Laurence Olivier, celebrated Shakespearean actor
taken as written

explanation.surface: A great actor swaps parts for a role in Twelfth Night.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Parts' suggests stage roles, but here it means letters: the final two of the actor's surname give way to A.
explanation.definitionFit: Olivia is the countess wooed by Orsino in Twelfth Night, who falls for the disguised Viola.

clue.text: Text for Macbeth, say, putting extra time into revised bit role

indicators.note: putting one thing into another places it inside
extra says this letter is an addition slipped in among the others
a revised text has been reworked, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A rewrite of Macbeth's script gives a minor part extra stage time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Macbeth' here is Verdi's opera, not Shakespeare's play.
explanation.definitionFit: A libretto is the written words of an opera, and Verdi's Macbeth is an example needing one.

clue.text: King not doing so well, such as Claudius or Richard III

definitions.text: such as Claudius or Richard III

parts.note: K is the chess abbreviation for king
more ill, in poorer health

explanation.surface: A sickly king, like Claudius or Richard III, is in declining health.
explanation.definitionFit: Claudius poisons his brother and Richard III has his nephews murdered: both are murderers.

clue.text: In kind way, nurse initially encouraging Romeo's love? Yes

parts.note: to nurse a patient is to tend them

indicators.note: initially points to the first letter of each of the following words

parts.note: first letters of the four words

explanation.surface: Juliet's Nurse gently encourages Romeo's love, confirming it with a yes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nurse' recalls Juliet's Nurse, but it is the verb meaning look after.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting tenderly means acting gently and with affection, which is a kind manner.
